decided: Under the program sign-off, a program counts as finished when every stage is archived, waiting for ratification, complete, or ended by the user, so a stage the user ended without archiving any change does not stop it. With the setting at its default, the existing end-of-program readout keeps reading every stage archived exactly as it is worded today; the difference between the two readings for an ended stage is written down as a known limit for the program's next architecture session to settle.
alternatives: read every stage archived as finished under every setting, which changes what users see with no setting changed
why: Nothing the user sees may change with every setting at its default, and a program that withdrew a stage must still be able to finish under the program sign-off.
